key_insight: Perfumer combines an LLM-based agent, predictive models and Quantum ESPRESSO to accelerate structural relaxation and predict electronic bands from natural-language requests.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce computation and workflow setup effort for first-principles materials screening.
method: Translate natural-language requests into structure-to-band workflows, using uploaded structures or automatically constructed candidates.
Pre-relax structures with Perfumer-relax, then refine them with Quantum ESPRESSO.
Predict 12 band energies at requested wavevectors using a periodic graph neural network and latent Hermitian spectral head that preserve reciprocal-lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2.75× overall relaxation speedup on tested structures; trained on 125,153 band structures, Perfumer-band achieved 0.157 eV median per-material MAE on 2,607 test materials from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, with inference taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores.
watch_item: The 12-band output and reported aggregate error warrant validation for target materials and properties requiring finer electronic-structure accuracy.
paper_title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
